subject: microbiology
title: Nagler Reaction, Lecithinase and Clostridium tetani

steps.tx: The **Nagler reaction** plates perfringens on egg yolk agar half spread with antitoxin: lecithinase splits yolk lecithin into opalescent precipitate around colonies only on the antitoxin free half, alpha toxin neutralised on the other, identifying C perfringens presumptively in hours. Egg yolk opacity is phospholipase made visible.
steps.say: Opalescence stops at the antitoxin border: Nagler neutralisation drawn on a plate.

left.title: Nagler setup
points: Egg yolk agar plate, half antitoxin spread
Pearl opalescence antitoxin free side only

right.title: Lecithinase cast
points: C bifermentans and sordellii weaker kin

steps.tx: **Clostridium tetani** is a slender anaerobic rod with terminal round spore (drumstick, tennis racket), swarming film growth, gelatin liquefier, toxin tetanospasmin maker, soil and gut spore ubiquitous, causing tetanus when spores germinate in anaerobic wounds (deep punctures, devitalised tissue, unclean deliveries and injections).
steps.say: Drumstick spores in soil plus a neglected wound equals tetanus risk.

left.title: Organism portrait
points: Terminal spherical spore wider than rod

right.title: Disease doorways
points: Chronic ulcers and otitis rare portals

steps.tx: **Tetanospasmin** travels retrogradely in motor axons (and blood to cord terminals) to inhibitory interneurons, cleaving synaptobrevin (VAMP) so glycine and GABA release fails and motor neurons fire unchecked: trismus, risus sardonicus, opisthotonos, spasms on stimuli, autonomic storms, consciousness preserved. The same VAMP cut botulinum performs peripherally to opposite sign.
steps.say: Cut the brake cables in the cord: spasms are disinhibition, not excitation.

left.title: Toxin journey
points: Produced at wound, binds nerve endings
Retrograde axonal transport to cord and brainstem
VAMP cleavage blocks glycine and GABA

right.title: Clinical grammar
points: Spatula test: biting instead of gag

steps.tx: **Tetanus management** is neutralise, clean, sedate, support: human tetanus immunoglobulin neutralises unbound toxin (intrathecal debated), wound debridement after HTIG, metronidazole (penicillin GABA antagonist theoretical disadvantage), benzodiazepine sedation escalating to paralysis and ventilation, autonomic management (magnesium, clonidine, morphine), immunisation because disease does not immunise.
steps.say: Immunoglobulin, debride, sedate deeply, ventilate long: tetanus care is supportive endurance.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepines, dark quiet room, minimise stimuli

steps.tx: **Tetanus prevention** is wound toilet plus toxoid: clean minor wounds need booster if over ten years (five for dirty), unknown or incomplete histories earn toxoid plus immunoglobulin for dirty wounds, neonatal tetanus falls with maternal immunisation and clean cord care, disease survivors still vaccinated because toxin dose that sickens does not immunise.
steps.say: The wound table (clean dirty by vaccine history) is tetanus prevention's whole algorithm.

left.title: Wound categories
points: Clean minor versus tetanus prone (deep, dirty, devitalised, puncture)
HTIG 250 IU for dirty wounds unimmunised

steps.tx: **Tetanus forms** specialise: generalised commonest, localised (rigidity near wound, may generalise), cephalic (head wound, cranial palsies, poor prognosis), neonatal (day 3 to 14, failure to suck then spasms), each with incubation and severity prognostication (short incubation worse), diagnosis clinical always (cultures rarely positive).
steps.say: Diagnosis is clinical; a negative wound culture never acquits tetanus.

left.title: Form map
points: Cephalic: cranial nerve palsies after head injury or otitis

right.title: Prognostic signs
points: Period of onset under 48 hours severe
Age extremes and portal (umbilical, uterine) worse

steps.tx: **Reverse CAMP** returns for anaerobes: perfringens beta haemolysis inhibits staphylococcal sphingomyelinase zone (arrow pointing away), separating it from group B streptococcus CAMP positive, one plate two directions examiners toggle between modules deliberately. Keeping both CAMP directions in one mental picture prevents the commonest interpretation error when a plate contains an unfamiliar haemolysis pattern.
steps.say: Arrow toward staph is group B, arrow suppressed is perfringens: reverse CAMP flips the lesson.

steps.tx: **Anaerobic bench details for tetani** (cooked meat medium growth, swarming film on blood agar, Fildes technique isolating by swarming edge, toxin mouse tests abandoned) explain why laboratories seldom confirm; prevention and clinical diagnosis carry tetanus therefore, documentation of immunisation status the audit metric.
steps.say: Isolation is hard and irrelevant acutely; immunisation records are the useful laboratory.
